corrected_record.support_text: The authors discuss a mouse study of emodin and explicitly state that its safety in humans cannot yet be concluded. Their mouse studies at 20, 40 and 80 mg/kg appeared safe under the tested conditions. Potential effects at higher human exposures remain unresolved; this passage supplies no tested human negative outcome.
corrected_record.qualifying_conditions: This is an author discussion in a mouse safety study, not a negative human clinical study. The animal findings are limited to the reported species, doses and duration; absence of human clinical data does not establish human safety.
corrected_record.extra_details: Hepatotoxic and mutagenic effects were reported only in experimental rodent studies at large doses; emodin lacks FDA approval and has limited human use as a marketed laxative/anti-cortisol dietary supplement. The paper explicitly states there is no evidence supporting hepatotoxic effects of emodin in humans at this time.

corrected_record.support_text: Loss of ΔΨm in K562 cells treated with 6.0 µM Q39 for 6–48 h in hypoxia was assessed with JC-1 staining, indicated by a switch from red to green fluorescence. Compared with the corresponding control, Q39 decreased ΔΨm in K562 cells after 12–48 h incubation in a time-dependent manner. Quantitative flow cytometry showed the percentages of cells with low ΔΨm increased nearly 10-fold in cells exposed to Q39 for 48 h compared with the corresponding control in hypoxia.

corrected_record.extra_details: Q39 is the quinoxaline 1,4-dioxide compound explicitly named in PMID 18215659. The tested system is hypoxic K562 leukemia cells. corrected_record.support_text: In the co-amoxiclav dosing cohort, hepatotoxicity occurred in 2 of 94 standard-regimen patients and 1 of 95 optimised-regimen patients (p=0.62). One standard-group case had ALT and bilirubin elevations; the other two cases had ALP and GGT elevations. These are combination-treatment observations.
corrected_record.qualifying_conditions: Adults with diabetic foot infection receiving intravenous co-amoxiclav. Standard group: 94 patients, 1.2 g every 8 h; optimised group: 95 patients, 1.2 g every 6 h. Outcomes belong to the combination treatment. The optimised group is not an untreated observation group. No individual-component causal attribution is established here.
corrected_record.extra_details: The paper reports two hepatotoxicity events in the standard group and one in the optimised group; the latter case has Naranjo +3 (possible), whereas the two standard-group cases have +5 (probable). Preserve these separate case attributions; do not assign probable status to the optimised-group case or an individual component.
